The Mental Health (MH) Clinical Operations Manager (COM) is located in the Mental Health Service under the Behavioral Health Interdisciplinary Program (BHIP) Program Manager at VA Northern California Health Care System.

The COM works in close collaboration with the MH Management Team to facilitate the logistical and operational needs across MH programs at their site. The Chico COM directly supervises a workforce of BHIP employees at the Chico and Yuba City clinics.

The COM helps to ensure that the Behavioral Health Interdisciplinary Program BHIP Team meets the overall performance standards, measures, and mission of the VA and the BHIP Program.

The COM ensures timely, integrated, efficient and effective delivery of MH services across the continuum of care for Veterans who are served at the Chico and Yuba City sites.

Duties for the position may include but are not limited to: Ensures efficient delivery of services related to BHIP program, involving both day-to-day operations and long-term planning and growth; Provides oversight to BHIP team operations in order to assure comprehensive provision of collaborative care; Provides local operational oversight around utilization, bookability, and performance metrics, assures grid accuracy and maintains DSS mapping to meet programmatic expectations; Supervises BHIP multidisciplinary staff, which may include psychiatrists, psychologists, advanced practice nurses, social workers, peer specialists, and program support assistants; Hires and trains all BHIP staff at as assigned site; Establishes guidelines and performance expectations for staff, which are clearly communicated through the formal employee performance management system; Provides feedback and periodically evaluates employee performance throughout the year; Resolves informal complaints and grievances; develops work improvement plans, recommending personnel actions as necessary; Effects disciplinary measures as appropriate to the authority delegated in this area; Reviews and approves or disapproves leave requests; Establishes and monitors clinic profiles in terms of availability, utilization and scheduling, and staff productivity; Attends site management meetings and serves as a liaison with delegated authority as needed to address site specific operational concerns; Works with the facility management to maintain a clear understanding of policy and up to date procedures concerning local safety issues, disaster planning, and related preparedness concerns; Communicates with other MH Managers and MH Administrative Officer regarding any space needs or issues at a given site.

This includes acting as the MH POC and MH liaison, directing issues to and reporting back from the appropriate authority; Coordinates with and serves as MH liaison to Telehealth, BDMS, Clinical Informatics, IT and other services as needed in order to facilitate efficient clinical operations and address local problems across programs; Completes assigned Performance Improvement activities at the program, service line and medical center level; Coordinates with facility management to assure that engineering and physical plant concerns are addressed in a timely manner; Provides public relations and community outreach and education regarding VA care to various social agencies, medical/primary care, legal, housing, and welfare organizations; Participates in root cause analysis and addresses action plan items related to patient safety and patient care issues.

Provides specialized psychological services at all levels of complexity for patients, with service delivery to include intake evaluation, diagnostic assessments, psychotherapy and patient education; Assesses and diagnoses mental disorders and conducts specialized psychological and/or cognitive function assessments and neuropsychological screenings; Treats mental disorders through a variety of modalities (and especially EBPs), and provides adjunctive interventions for treatment of medical disorders; Provides a full range of therapeutic interventions including individual and group psychotherapy, family therapy, consultation, rehabilitation and psychoeducation; Participates on selection panels for Staff Psychologist position vacancies or other positions as assigned by Chief MHPL.

Other related duties as assigned. Work Schedule: Monday - Friday; 8:00 a.m. - 4:30 p.m.; Tour of duty subject to change to meet the needs of the Agency Telework: Available ad hoc as per agency policy Virtual: This is not a virtual position.

Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy.

Education: Doctoral degree in psychology from a graduate program in psychology accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA), the Psychological Clinical Science Accreditation System (PCSAS), or the Canadian Psychological Association (CPA) at the time the program was completed.

The specialty area of the degree must be consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

OR Have a doctoral degree in any area of psychology and, in addition, successfully complete a respecialization program (including documentation of an approved internship completed as part of the respecialization program) meeting both of the following conditions: the respecialization program must be completed in an APA or a CPA accredited doctoral program; and the specialty in which the applicant is retrained must be consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

NOTE: The applicant must provide an official transcript and/or certificate documenting the completion of the respecialization program, which includes completion of an APA or CPA internship. OR Have a doctoral degree awarded between 1951 and 1978 from a regionally-accredited institution, with a dissertation primarily psychological in nature.

Internship: Have successfully completed a professional psychology internship training program that was accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed and that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

OR New VHA psychology internship programs that are in the process of applying for APA accreditation are acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement, provided that such programs were sanctioned by the VHA Central Office Program Director for Psychology and the VHA Office of Academic Affiliations at the time that the individual was an intern; OR VHA facilities that offered full-time, one-year pre-doctoral internships prior to PL 96-151 (pre-1979) are considered to be acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement; OR Applicants who completed an internship that was not accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed may be considered eligible for hire only if they are currently board certified by the American Board of Professional Psychology in a specialty area that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

(NOTE: Once board certified, the employee is required to maintain board certification.) OR Applicants who have a doctoral degree awarded between 1951 and 1978 from a regionally-accredited institution with a dissertation primarily psychological in nature may fulfill this internship requirement by having the equivalent of a one-year supervised internship experience in a site specifically acceptable to the candidate's doctoral program.

If the internship experience is not noted on the applicant's official transcript, the applicant must provide a statement from the doctoral program verifying that the equivalent of a one-year supervised internship experience was completed in a site acceptable to the doctoral program.

Licensure: Hold a full, current, and unrestricted license to practice psychology at the doctoral level in a State, Territory, or Commonwealth of the United States, or the District of Columbia.

Exception: Non-licensed applicants who otherwise meet the eligibility requirements may be given a temporary appointment as a "graduate psychologist" at the GS-11 or GS-12 grade under the authority of 38 U.S.C. 7405 [(c)(2)(B)] for a period not to exceed two years from the date of employment on the condition that such a psychologist provide care only under the supervision of a psychologist who is licensed.

Failure to obtain licensure during that period is justification for termination of the temporary appointment.

Please indicate clearly on your cv/resume or cover letter what your current licensure status is, and if unlicensed where you are in the process of obtaining your license.(e.g., "Passed EPPP 6/2020, CA state exam scheduled 10/15/21") English Language Proficiency: Psychologists must be proficient in spoken and written English in accordance with VA Handbook 5005, Part II, Chapter 3, section A, paragraph 3j.

May qualify based on being covered by the Grandfathering Provision as described in the VA Qualification Standard for this occupation (only applicable to current VHA employees who are in this occupation and meet the criteria). Grade Determinations: Psychology Program Manager, GS-14 (a) Experience.

At least three years of experience as a professional psychologist, with at least one year equivalent to the GS-13 grade level. (b) Demonstrated Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities. In addition to the experience above, the candidate must demonstrate all of the following KSAs: 1.

Ability to organize work, set priorities, delegate tasks, and meet multiple deadlines. 2. Knowledge of and ability to utilize evidence based practices and clinical practice guidelines appropriately and ability to guide staff in using these tools. 3.

Ability to deal effectively with individuals or groups representing widely divergent backgrounds, interests, and points of view. 4. Skill in managing and directing the work of others to accomplish program goals and objectives. 5. Ability to translate management goals and objectives into well-coordinated and controlled work operations. 6.

Ability to establish and monitor production and performance priorities and standards. 7. Ability to analyze organizational and operational problems and to develop and implement solutions that result in sound operation of the program. References: VA Handbook 5005, Chapter II, Appendix G39. The full performance level of this vacancy is GS-14.

## Description de l'entreprise ##
Avec plus de 13'000 collaborateurs et collaboratrices représentant 160 métiers, les Hôpitaux Universitaires de Genève sont un établissement de référence au niveau national et international. Pour en savoir plus sur notre institution, prenez quelques minutes pour consulter notre rétrospective 2025 en cliquant ici.
La Direction des soins incarne l-autorité en matière de soins. Elle a pour mission de garantir la qualité et la sécurité des soins au sein de l'établissement. A ce titre, la Direction des soins a droit de regard sur l-ensemble des activités des soins (infirmiers, infirmières et différents corps professionnels de santé).

Pour remplir sa mission, elle s-appuie sur trois pôles d'expertises : qualité, durabilité et innovation digitale ; expertise clinique et pratiques professionnelles ; management et transformation.
## Description du poste ##
La direction des soins est à la recherche de son ou sa future responsable diététicienne pour manager et accompagner les équipes sur le site de Cluse-Roseraie dans leurs prestations dans différents départements médicaux. La patientèle peut être adulte comme pédiatrique notamment dans le domaine des soins aigus ainsi que pour l-enseignement thérapeutique au décours de la maladie chronique.
Vous dirigez une équipe d-environ 30 collaborateurs et collaboratrices. Vous organisez, coordonnez et supervisez leurs activités et prévoyez toute action nécessaire de développement des compétences individuelles comme collectives. Vous garantissez une circulation optimale des informations, qu-elle soit ascendante, descendante et/ ou transversale. Vous développez un climat de confiance dans l-équipe nécessaire au bien vivre et travailler ensemble dans le respect des valeurs institutionnelles.
Vous savez donner le cap et accompagner vos équipes pour atteindre des objectifs communs. Vous déclinez les axes stratégiques de votre métier en objectifs réalisables par l-équipe tout en veillant à la contribution individuelle de chaque membre.
En qualité de responsable d-équipe, vous êtes garante ou garant de la qualité des soins nutritionnels et promouvez toute mesure visant à optimiser et à améliorer les prestations offertes à la patientèle. Vous disposez d-indicateurs pour conduire l-amélioration continue de la qualité. Vous contribuez également au développement de nouvelles pratiques.
Votre esprit collaboratif vous permet de soutenir et développer l-interdisciplinarité entre tous les professionnelles et professionnels de la santé agissant sur la prise en charge des patientes et patients.
Vous gérez aisément la bonne allocation des ressources comme du matériel pour répondre aux besoins en soins des patients et patientes dans le cadre du budget alloué. Vous exercez également un rôle de référente ou référent pour les systèmes tarifaires en lien avec la profession
Selon les besoins, vous êtes amené ou amenée à recruter de nouvelles collaboratrices et collaborateurs et veillez au développement de leur expertise dans les champs de spécialité de chaque secteur tout en veillant à la polyvalence nécessaire des compétences

Vous êtes titulaire d'un Bachelor HES en nutrition et diététique ou d'un titre jugé équivalent, reconnu par la Croix-Rouge suisse.
Vous bénéficiez d'une expérience confirmée en management, acquise au travers d'au moins cinq années de pratique dans le domaine hospitalier. Une formation en management, telle qu'un CAS en management des institutions de santé, constitue un atout.
Dotée ou doté d'excellentes qualités relationnelles, vous faites preuve d'entregent et d'une communication positive. Vous savez fédérer les équipes autour d'objectifs communs et instaurer un climat de collaboration propice au bon fonctionnement du service.
Ouvert ou ouverte au changement, vous êtes capable d'accompagner les évolutions de votre environnement professionnel avec pragmatisme. Vous savez également prendre du recul sur vos pratiques managériales afin de les faire évoluer de manière continue.
Vous êtes une personne reconnue pour votre sens de l'organisation, votre flexibilité et votre capacité à gérer les priorités, vous êtes à l'aise dans un environnement où les activités sont variées et transversales.
Vous maîtrisez les outils informatiques courants et possédez une excellente maîtrise de la langue française.

As a member of the ASPCA ’s Project Management Office—part of the Strategy Team—the Senior Project Manager plays a key role in advancing the ASPCA ’s mission through thoughtful planning, coordination, and execution.
This individual partners across the organization to provide structure and accountability for complex initiatives, ensuring projects are delivered on time, within scope, and in alignment with our core value of TEAM. This role is ideal for a highly organized and collaborative project management professional who excels at connecting strategy to execution, leading teams through change, and driving successful outcomes for high-impact organizational initiatives.
Who We Are
At the ASPCA , our Strategy team plays a vital role in advancing the organization’s mission to improve the lives of animals through good welfare. We work across programs and partners to spark innovation, strengthen sheltering systems, and drive meaningful, measurable impact. Our team brings together experts in strategy, planning, project portfolio management, research, and impact measurement—each dedicated to helping the ASPCA deliver its highest priorities with clarity, alignment, and purpose.
As part of this group, the Project Management Office (PMO) serves as a strategic engine for execution. Established in 2021, the PMO provides centralized oversight of the ASPCA ’s project portfolio, ensuring that resources, attention, and efforts are focused where they can drive the greatest value.

Through a robust portfolio management framework, the PMO promotes strategic agility, supports dynamic resource alignment, and streamlines delivery so teams can stay focused on improving outcomes for animals.
Together, the Strategy team and PMO foster a collaborative, mission‑driven environment where big ideas become actionable plans, cross‑functional partnerships thrive, and complex challenges are tackled with creativity and discipline. We’re united by a shared commitment to making a measurable difference for animals—and the people who care for them.

The Senior Project Manager, Project Management Office plays a critical role in supporting the successful delivery of enterprise initiatives that advance the ASPCA ’s Strategic Framework. This individual partners closely with project sponsors, team leaders, and cross-functional stakeholders to ensure projects are planned, organized, and executed with clarity, accountability, and consistency.
The ideal candidate brings strong project management expertise, exceptional organizational skills, and the ability to coordinate multiple complex initiatives simultaneously. A successful Senior Project Manager combines sharp critical thinking and problem-solving abilities with a collaborative, solutions-oriented mindset. This individual understands how strategic priorities translate into operational work, takes ownership of outcomes, and is able to adapt and pivot when circumstances change. They bring creativity, compassion, and a commitment to continuous improvement, ensuring projects are delivered with excellence and lasting impact.

OR, have a doctoral degree in any area of psychology and, in addition, successfully completed a re-specialization program meeting both of the following conditions: a) the re-specialization program must be completed in an APA or a CPA accredited doctoral program; and b) the specialty in which you were retrained is consistent with the assignment you are am applying for; OR, have a doctoral degree awarded between 1951 and 1978 from a regionally-accredited institution, with a dissertation primarily psychological in nature.

Internship Requirement - You must have successfully completed a professional psychology internship training program that was accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed and that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed; OR, New VHA psychology internship programs that are in the process of applying for APA accreditation are acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement, provided that such programs were sanctioned by the VHA Central Office Program Director for Psychology and the VHA Office of Academic Affiliations at the time that the individual was an intern; OR, VHA facilities that offered full-time, one-year pre-doctoral internships prior to PL 96-151 (pre-1979) are considered to be acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement; OR, Applicants who completed an internship that was not accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed may be considered eligible for hire only if they are currently board certified by the American Board of Professional Psychology in a specialty area that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

Psychologist program managers have broad program management responsibilities for a specific program or programs that are designed to deliver specialized, complex, highly professional services that are important program components of the facility and that significantly impact the health care provided to Veterans.

Programs include but are not limited to addiction, posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), mental health intensive case management (MHICM), mental health compensation and pension examination (C&P) programs, Psychosocial Rehabilitation and Recovery Centers, inpatient mental health, residential rehabilitation, domiciliary, palliative care, neuropsychology, and internship and postdoctoral fellowship training programs; management of an off campus site; psychology program oversight and coordination throughout the facility and its affiliated clinics as a psychology executive, typically at lower complexity facilities.

Responsibilities include operation and management of key clinical, training, research, or administrative programs to include full responsibility for managing the day to day activities of those programs. Responsibility may include supervision of staff but is not required.

s.h: About the role and what you will be doing
s.t:
The Senior Project Manager provides senior-level expertise to plan, organise, control, and deliver large, complex infrastructure and data centre migration projects across Ensono's client portfolio.

Operating within the Global Project and Implementation (GPI) practice, this role manages multiple company-wide initiatives simultaneously — from scope definition and budget planning through to delivery and post-implementation review.

A key part of this position involves building and maintaining strong relationships with client sponsors and internal leaders, including regular on-site engagement at the client's London office.

The Senior Project Manager interfaces directly with client executive management to understand critical business priorities and ensures every project is completed within agreed scope, quality, time, and cost constraints.

· Collaborate with stakeholders to ensure business requirements are clearly defined, understood, and documented

· Define project scope, risks, potential issues, and resource requirements at the outset of each engagement

· Ensure project benefits are realised while managing the impact of organisational change on the business and its clients

· Develop project phases and translate them into clear, measurable project plans

· Communicate internally and externally on delivery of work products, planning activities, and cross-organisational resource relationships

· Manage projects in full adherence to Ensono's project management methodology

· Manage project scope across mission, objectives, and requirements throughout the project lifecycle

· Manage project schedules, including key milestone dates and critical path tracking

· Lead the team in identifying project risks, issues, assumptions, and dependencies; act as the primary escalation point and drive effective mitigation strategies to maintain project goals

· Provide leadership and strategic direction to the project team across all phases of delivery

· Oversee all project work streams, including timeline adherence, quality of deliverables, risk management, issue escalation, and stakeholder collaboration

· Work with all stakeholders to ensure governance frameworks and continuous improvement or transformation plans are established and maintained

· Establish deadlines, assign tasks, and monitor and summarise project progress for all relevant parties

· Develop business insights through analysis of results and communicate key findings to management to support data-driven decision-making

· Secure appropriate resources and personnel in collaboration with management to ensure projects are delivered on time and within budget

· Escalate barriers, risks, and issues that may impact timelines or deliverables in a timely and appropriate manner

· Manage the development of polished executive-level presentations and deliver findings to internal associates and external clients clearly and concisely

· Manage project status reporting in line with prescribed timelines for each engagement

· Develop measurement processes and methods to assess progress towards project goals and outcomes

· Manage project costs and budgets throughout the full delivery lifecycle

· Facilitate cross-training to support job rotation and minimise gaps in assignment coverage

· Provide coaching and constructive feedback to all project team members

· Mentor less experienced associates within the project management practice

· Interface with client executive management on-site at the client's London office to understand and address critical business issues and concerns

· Proficient in MS Office and MS Project

· Strong financial management skills, including experience with project budgeting and cost control

· Effective team management skills with the ability to lead matrixed, cross-functional teams

· Strong leadership and strategic direction capabilities

· IT outsourcing knowledge

· Strong infrastructure management experience

· ITIL and/or ITSM knowledge

· Ability to organise and define work in complex or ambiguous situations

· Ability to travel to the client's office in London as required

· Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment

· Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Management Information Systems (MIS), or equivalent experience

· Minimum of 7 years of complex IT programme and project management experience

· Demonstrated experience managing large-scale infrastructure and data centre migration projects

· MBA or Bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, or Engineering preferred

· Project financial and revenue recognition experience preferred

## Description de l'emploi ##
L'Unité organisation territoriale (UOT) de la Direction générale de la cohésion sociale (DGCS), contribue à la réflexion et au pilotage de l'organisation des prestations sociales sur le territoire cantonal.

Elle analyse les besoins des différentes régions, coordonne les acteurs concernés et accompagne la mise en œuvre et l'évolution des dispositifs sociaux, en veillant à leur cohérence et à leur accessibilité pour la population.

Elle a également pour mission d'assurer une vision cohérente transverse pour le parc immobilier subventionné par la DGCS qui comprend notamment l'hébergement médico-social (EMS, EPSM, ESE) et les ateliers à vocation productive, soit environ 400 bâtiments gérés par 250 partenaires.
Afin de mener un projet ambitieux visant à établir une stratégie pour la mise aux normes énergétiques et d'adaptation aux conséquences du réchauffement climatique du parc immobilier de la structure socio-sanitaire, l'Unité organisation territoriale (UOT) recherche **un·e Chef·fe de projet Plan climat.**
Pour de plus amples informations, veuillez consulter le cahier des charges en cliquant ici ou contacter Monsieur Mathieu Capcarrère, Conseiller stratégique, à l'adresse email: dgcs.recrutement@vd.ch
## Responsabilités ##
* Structurer et mettre en place de la phase 1 du projet DSAS-1 du plan climat vaudois de 2ème génération œuvrant à faire un état des lieux du parc immobilier accueillant des populations vulnérables et subventionné par la DGCS.
* Piloter la phase 1 du projet DSAS-1 du plan climat vaudois (EMPD 24 LEG 168) et en assurer l-avancement selon le calendrier prévu et l-enveloppe budgétaire dédiée.
* Conseiller, renseigner et appuyer les mandataires externes, les interlocuteur·trice·s internes, et les partenaires impliqués dans le projet DSAS-1 du plan climat vaudois.
* Initier et piloter la phase 2 du projet DSAS-1 du plan climat vaudois en définissant et mettant en œuvre un ou plusieurs projets pilotes liés à la transition énergétique, à la durabilité et au climat, sur la base des résultats et analyses de la phase 1.
* Coconstruire les réflexions avec l-équipe UOT sur les questions de transition énergétique, durabilité et climat, et être activement partie prenante aux réflexions collectives de l-équipe et du service sur ces thématiques.

* Formation en gestion de projet souhaitée.
* Formation en analyse de parc immobilier exigée.
* Formation en expertise de la transition énergétique, un atout.
* Expérience professionnelle de 8 ans minimum dans la coordination d'équipe pluridisciplinaire et dans la gestion de projet.
* Solides connaissances des procédures de mises en concurrence selon les marchés publics.
* Bonnes compétences dans l'organisation d'octroi de mandats.
* Sens des responsabilités et éthique du service public.
* Capacité d'organisation, de gestion du temps, d'adaptation et de flexibilité.
* Écoute et communication.
* Bonne expression orale et esprit d'entraide et de collaboration.
* Vision globale et sens de la perspective.

Deine Aufgaben
Technische Projektleitung von A bis Z: Du verantwortest Neu\- und Umbauprojekte von Anlagen, Systemen oder Baugruppen am Standort Istighofen von der ersten Idee über die Ausschreibung und Realisierung bis hin zur finalen Abschlusskontrolle hinsichtlich Leistung, Qualität, Terminen und Budget.

Amazon Extra Large (AMXL) is a single-threaded organization that owns the end-to-end customer experience for heavy and bulky products, from supply chain and fulfillment through transportation, last mile delivery, and post-purchase resolution. AMXL currently operates across North America, Europe, Japan, and is expanding into emerging markets.

Within AMXL, the CX and Growth org is a centralized, worldwide team organized across five pillars designed to ensure that every customer who purchases a large, high-value product receives a reliable experience.
The Execution Excellence pillar is where planning meets the customer. It houses two complementary teams: our AMXL Operations Center and our AMXL Proactive Execution program.

These teams serve as the real-time network execution backbone, translating strategic decisions into daily network performance across our end-to-end network and also as the mechanism that identifies delivery failures before they become visible to the customer and intervenes proactively to save the delivery or manage the recovery directly with the customer.

Together, these teams form a closed loop: detect upstream, prevent where possible, intervene proactively where not, and feed root causes back so defects are resolved at the source.
We are seeking a Senior Program Manager to lead the integration and transformation of this combined organization. This is not a steady-state program management role. The program strategy is being built.

You will inherit a consolidation in progress and own the lifecycle of making it work: assessing what the combined org should look like, defining how we measure success, building the mechanisms that make it sustainable, and driving the hard conversations required to get there.

You will use process lifecycle evaluation methodologies to categorize the team's portfolio (automate, simplify, reallocate, or deprecate), and build automation roadmaps in partnership with technical teams.
This role requires someone who can operate in high ambiguity, make trade-offs between short-term operational needs and long-term strategic goals, and communicate persuasively across teams. The right candidate sees automation and AI as something they use today, not something they plan to use later, and will set the standard for how this team uses technology to scale impact without scaling headcount.

· Define the operating model for the combined organization: org design, process rationalization, scope definition, and mechanisms that make it self-sustaining.
· Build the process lifecycle evaluation framework, determining which workflows to automate, simplify, reallocate, or retire, and manage the pipeline of new use cases from scoping through launch.
· Own the automation roadmap in partnership with data science, engineering, and technology teams, establishing accountability mechanisms with clear timelines for every manual process.
· Drive cross-functional stakeholder alignment across supply chain, quality, and operations, navigating complex organizational dynamics and building trust where needed.
· Scale this capability into new geographies by adapting the operating model to local carrier ecosystems, regulatory environments, and workforce availability.
A day in the life
You might start your morning reviewing program metrics dashboards, identifying areas that need attention, and preparing a status narrative for a director-level review. By mid-morning you are facilitating a working session with partners to align on priorities for the quarter.

After lunch you dive into data to validate assumptions behind a proposed solution, then draft a decision document that frames trade-offs for leadership. You close the day mentoring a newer program manager and connecting with cross-regional counterparts to keep workstreams on track.

· **Eliminate**: detect, solve, and resolve customer-impacting issues upstream by providing relevant and timely insights for operations teams, transportation, and product development.
· **Automate**: continuously assess and identify opportunities to replace manual processes with automated, scalable solutions.
· **Optimize**: when a customer does need support, ensure AMXL stakeholders have the tools, resources, policies, and protocols to deliver a perfect experience.
The operations center translates strategic decisions into daily network performance. The proactive execution team ensures that when defects occur, customers are protected through early intervention. The Sr. Program Manager will be the link that makes both teams operate as one system.
